targets: multi-agent LLM trading coordination (Axelrod / reputation / coalitions)

papers.title: PolySwarm: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Prediction Market Trading and Latency Arbitrage
papers.abstract_snippet: Production-ready multi-agent LLM trading terminal that deploys 50 diverse LLM personas on Polymarket. Probability aggregation via confidence-weighted Bayesian combination; KL and Jensen-Shannon divergence drive an information-theoretic cross-market inefficiency detector. Quarter-Kelly sizing. Swarm aggregation consistently outperforms single-model baselines on Brier, calibration, and log-loss vs human superforecasters.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: Direct blueprint for a 5th Polymarket Trading Floor — confirms our 17-agent approach is aligned with SOTA; quarter-Kelly matches MIN_DEPLOY_PCT floor doctrine; KL/JS divergence is a drop-in anti-lockstep signal we do not yet compute.
papers.implementation_complexity: medium (2-3 weeks: port divergence engine to existing TF app.py, wire py-clob-client)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: POL fleet: -0.003 Brier (KL-aware ensemble weighting on POL TF). PM-TF (new): $5-15k/mo paper-trade if we survive 30 days at their calibration level.
papers.kill_criterion: If paper-trade PM-TF loses >20% on rolling 30-day window vs random baseline, shelve.

papers.title: Coalition Formation in LLM Agent Networks: Stability Analysis and Convergence Guarantees
papers.abstract_snippet: First framework grounding coalition formation in LLM agent networks in hedonic game theory. Introduces the LLM Coalition Formation Game (LCFG) with Nash-stable partition sufficient conditions. Coalition-of-Thought (CoalT) protocol: 73.2% Nash-stable (vs 58.4% CoT, 41.8% standard prompting; p<0.001). 2,400 episodes across GPT-4, Claude-3, Llama-3.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: Directly addresses the Apr 18 bug where 0/16 agents emitted coalition_proposal. CoalT prompt protocol is a drop-in replacement for AXELROD_CANON — promises 73.2% stable coalitions vs our post-fix 'MANDATORY' which still yields ~20-30% coalition adoption.
papers.implementation_complexity: low (3-5 days: port CoalT prompt template into coalition_block of both TFs; measure Nash-stability of produced pacts)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: Reduces lockstep Jaccard from 0.94 → target 0.65; expected PoL/NBA TF drawdown -25% when coalitions actually bind.
papers.kill_criterion: If post-CoalT audit shows <50% Nash-stable partitions after 10 days, revert.

papers.title: Risk-Constrained Kelly for Mutually Exclusive Outcomes: CRRA Support Invariance and Logarithmic One-Dimensional Calibration
papers.abstract_snippet: Proves that under the standard overround + unique likelihood-ratio prefix hypothesis, the drawdown-constrained Kelly optimizer has EXACTLY the same active set as the unconstrained problem. For log utility, reduces to a 1-D calibration: one outer scalar equation + independent 1-D inner solves on active states. Support invariance under both CRRA parameter γ and drawdown surrogate λ.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: This is the formal proof we were looking for when we shipped dynamic MIN_DEPLOY_PCT today (0.75→0.25 by drawdown). Instead of heuristic tiers, we can solve the 1-D calibration exactly. Active-set invariance means we only need to tune λ per-agent, not re-pick the bets.
papers.implementation_complexity: medium (1 week: implement scalar outer solver in tf_stake_sizer.py — scipy.optimize.brentq on outer + independent 1-D inner solves)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: PQTF / ITF / NBA: -30% max-drawdown at same expected growth rate; Sharpe +0.3 (from theory).
papers.kill_criterion: If post-replacement paper Sharpe < pre-replacement for 14 days, revert to heuristic tiers.

papers.title: PolyBench: Benchmarking LLM Forecasting and Trading Capabilities on Live Prediction Market Data
papers.abstract_snippet: Multimodal benchmark fusing synchronized CLOB snapshots + news + binary market data. 38,666 markets / 4,997 events / 36,165 predictions over Feb 6-12 2026. Seven SOTA LLMs evaluated. TOP RESULTS: MiMo-V2-Flash 17.6% CWR, Gemini-3-Flash 6.2% CWR; other 5 models NEGATIVE despite high stated confidence. Order-book-realistic execution simulator.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: This is the evaluation harness we need BEFORE launching PM-TF. MiMo-V2-Flash + Gemini-3-Flash as top models — both already in our gateway routing plan. Gemini-3-Flash currently powers POL TF T4/T5 so we have a proxy for their 6.2% CWR.
papers.implementation_complexity: low (2-3 days: clone their code, run our own fleet as an 8th baseline)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: Produces an external-calibrated ranking card for Nomos42 LLM fleet; no direct PnL but de-risks PM-TF launch.
papers.kill_criterion: If our fleet scores below all 7 PolyBench models on CWR, kill PM-TF proposal.

papers.title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
papers.abstract_snippet: Advanced LLMs CONSISTENTLY DEFECT in single-shot social dilemmas — directly contradicts Axelrod 'never be first to defect'. Four mechanisms tested: (1) repeated play (2) reputation (3) third-party mediators (4) binding contracts with conditional payments. Finding: CONTRACTS + MEDIATION are most effective; reputation alone underperforms.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: Contradicts our prior (AXELROD_CANON assumes reputation is sufficient). Should add (a) binding contracts with conditional payments (pacts that auto-execute stake transfers when tripwire met) and (b) a T_MEDIATOR role — possibly qwen-235B moderator — which we already have as morning council but don't use mid-day.
papers.implementation_complexity: medium (1 week: port conditional-payment pact mechanics to coalition_proposal schema; make moderator mid-day arbiter on drawdown trips)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: Cooperation rate from ~0-10% (current single-shot-style prompting) → 40-60% (per their Fig 4); drawdown -15% indirect.
papers.kill_criterion: If binding-contract pacts have <30% execution rate after 14 days, revert.

papers.title: Classifier Calibration at Scale: An Empirical Study of Model-Agnostic Post-Hoc Methods
papers.abstract_snippet: 5 post-hoc calibrators × 21 classifier architectures on TabArena-v0.1. RANKING by log-loss: Venn-Abers > Beta > Isotonic ≈ Platt > Pearsonify. KEY RED FLAG: Platt scaling and isotonic regression SYSTEMATICALLY DEGRADE proper scoring performance on strong modern tabular models (CatBoost/XGBoost/LightGBM).
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: Our fleet best (S22 venn_abers_fusion 0.22073) confirms Venn-Abers wins — matches paper's #1. BUT: their data suggests isotonic (used on S14/S15/S17) may be DEGRADING Brier. Should audit all islands and switch isotonic→Beta/Venn-Abers on CatBoost/XGBoost/LightGBM islands.
papers.implementation_complexity: low (2 days: swap calibrator in init/mutate, ship via SWISH one island at a time)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: Fleet mean Brier: 0.22447 → target 0.22100 (0.0035 improvement, ~1.5%); S22-style gains applied fleet-wide.
papers.kill_criterion: If any swapped island loses >0.003 Brier in 48h walk-forward, revert.

papers.title: Inferring Latent Market Forces: Evaluating LLM Detection of Gamma Exposure Patterns via Obfuscation Testing
papers.abstract_snippet: LLMs achieve 71.5% detection rate on dealer-hedging/gamma-positioning/0DTE patterns using unbiased prompts (raw gamma values, no regime labels). With regime labels → 100%. WHO-WHOM-WHAT causal framework. 91.2% accuracy despite quarterly profitability variations. CRITICAL CAVEAT: detection ≠ profitability (Sharpe 1.8 → 0.1 in backtest).
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: ITF GammaOptions persona (mistral:large) should get the WHO-WHOM-WHAT prompt frame. The 'detection ≠ profitability' finding is important — warn PIXEL/accountant not to cite GEX pattern hits as alpha without realized PnL gate.
papers.implementation_complexity: low (3 days: WHO-WHOM-WHAT frame injection into GammaOptions system_prompt)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: ITF options leg: unclear PnL (their Sharpe drop is a warning). Primary value = better prompt structure.
papers.kill_criterion: If GammaOptions 0DTE PnL goes negative over 10 trading days, disable and revert.

papers.title: ATLAS: Adaptive Trading with LLM AgentS Through Dynamic Prompt Optimization and Multi-Agent Coordination
papers.abstract_snippet: Adaptive-OPRO: prompt-optimization that dynamically adapts using real-time stochastic feedback. Consistently outperforms fixed prompts across LLM families and regime-specific equity studies. Reflection-based feedback showed limited improvement — Adaptive-OPRO is the winner. Order-aware action space ensures executable trades.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: Directly extends our prompt-mutator (shipped 2026-04-19). Their Adaptive-OPRO uses stochastic feedback — we currently use binary post-mortem flags. Upgrade prompt_mutator.py to use realized PnL as stochastic reward signal rather than just failure flags.
papers.implementation_complexity: medium (1 week: upgrade prompt_mutator.py with OPRO-style stochastic-reward gradient, keep post-mortem as sanity check)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: TF agents: +8-12% cumulative return over 30 days (paper claim on SPY, we expect half).
papers.kill_criterion: If ACL-cited improvement not reproduced in 30d paper-trade, revert.

papers.title: When Valid Signals Fail: Regime Boundaries Between LLM Features and RL Trading Policies
papers.abstract_snippet: LLM-extracted features from news/filings achieve IC > 0.15 on held-out data (genuine predictive validity), YET 'valid intermediate representations do not automatically translate into downstream task performance'. During macroeconomic distribution shifts, LLM features ADD NOISE → underperform price-only baseline. Macro state variables remain most robust.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: Red flag for our 71-instrument ITF + POL-macro-1 proposal. Should ADD a regime detector (VIX > 25 or FRED macro-surprise > 1σ) that falls back to price-only ensemble, per their finding.
papers.implementation_complexity: medium (4-6 days: add regime_detector.py + fallback logic in all 4 TFs)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: Drawdown -20% during macro-stress periods (preservation gain, not alpha gain).
papers.kill_criterion: If regime detector trips >30% of trading days, recalibrate thresholds or remove.

papers.title: From Competition to Coordination: Market Making as a Scalable Framework for Safe and Aligned Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract_snippet: Each agent = market participant trading PROBABILISTIC BELIEFS to converge on shared truth. Economic incentive alignment without centralized oversight. +10% accuracy over single-shot baselines on factual reasoning / ethical judgment / commonsense inference.
papers.relevance_to_nomos42: Elegant upgrade path for morning council: agents currently 'propose' — here they would TRADE beliefs through an internal LMSR market, producing a natural calibration via market prices. Fits our fleet like a glove.
papers.implementation_complexity: high (2-3 weeks: internal LMSR order book for agent beliefs, then pipe to external betting)
papers.expected_Brier_or_PnL_delta: Brier -0.002 to -0.004 from natural calibration (their +10% accuracy maps roughly there).
papers.kill_criterion: If internal belief-market slows TF daily cycle > 2× baseline, shelve.
